label: copy-phase input j, late in the copy
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only when the fed-back input token is j (j inputs hold 97.6% of activation mass; i and h get small leftover activations). It never fires in the original phase or at the delimiter, even when j is input there. Firing is strongly tied to position: the rate on copy-phase j inputs goes up with t / recall_idx (about 0 before recall 3, then 3% of all steps at t=16-17), and longer sequences (L=8,9) hold most of the mass. The top activations are j inputs at recall_idx 6-7. The predicate catches about 95% of mass but only about 36% precision, since many copy-phase j inputs at mid positions stay silent. A stricter position cutoff (t >= 14) trades recall for precision (F1 about 0.61), so the feature behaves like a graded "j input x lateness" detector more than a sharp rule. It does not depend on first token, the next output, or digit count.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: j, i, h, p, r, u; least: e, b, c, w) and the token being output (most: j, p, i, h, r, 1; least: a, -, q, w); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=7, t=17, recall_idx=8.
